story: Gary is content at his workbench, powering up a speaker and testing its sound at a low volume, while Donna eagerly makes her way over to his house. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal sets off with quiet determination, and back at her dining table Rosa, worried but practical, looks over the leftover food and table settings. She is putting the pork away and weighing whether the dinner should be rescheduled.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Power up the speaker and test the sound levels at low volume
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa (rosa dining table): Look over the table settings and leftover food, put the pork away, and figure out whether to reschedule the dinner

gary.thought_process: I'm home on a sunny Sunday morning with nobody around. The memories say I filed the golf cart modification form at the review desk, so I'm covered on L-01, and I've already mounted the light strips and secured the speaker wiring. Donna is picking me up at 7:45 tomorrow for the ladder, so there's no rush on her. What's left is making sure the sound system actually works before parade day. Time to power it up at the workbench and test it, keeping the volume modest since it's a quiet Sunday morning, well after the 7 AM cutoff but still polite to the neighbors.

parameters.content: Power up the speaker and test the sound levels at low volume

donna.thought_process: I just arrived on Magnolia Loop with my pickleball bag and the spare paddle packed for Gary. Nobody is in line-of-sight, so I can't talk to anyone from here. Gary's house is connected and my plan is to pick him up and get him to the rec center for practice on court one. Talking is done for now, so the useful move is to walk to his place and collect him.

parameters.content: Heading to Gary's to pick him up for pickleball practice, spare paddle in the bag.

hal.thought_process: Logged the violations last tick, and nobody's around to talk to. My goal is getting these complaints in front of the architectural review committee, and Town Hall is the only place to do that. But Town Hall isn't connected to my house, so I have to go out to Magnolia Loop first. Might as well keep watch on the Loop while I'm out there, and see whether Donna's flock has thinned or Gary's cart is still lit up like a parade float.

parameters.content: Heading out to the Loop to check on Donna's flamingos and Gary's cart, then on toward Town Hall to file my complaints.

rosa.thought_process: It's Sunday, 9:17 AM, and my memories say I was waiting on a dinner that nobody showed up to. I checked my shift schedule twice and still seem unsure whether I got the date wrong. I'm back at my own house now and no one is nearby. The dinner may not have been tonight at all, so I shouldn't spiral. The most practical step is to go look at the dining table and kitchen: see what's actually sitting there, and then decide whether to reschedule. Before that, since no one's in line-of-sight, the best use of this tick is to deal with the food and the table, then go knock on doors in magnolia_loop later. For now, I'll check the dining table to figure out where things stand.

parameters.content: Look over the table settings and leftover food, put the pork away, and figure out whether to reschedule the dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
